extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing ERC grant proposals (Starting/Consolidator/Advanced/Synergy) and their host institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for preparing and submitting ERC grant proposals (StG, CoG, AdG, SyG) under the 2026 Work Programme, including eligibility, proposal structure, evaluation criteria and common weaknesses to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: Excellence (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: One Evaluation Criteria: Excellence composed of two dimensions — (1) Research Project and (2) Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence is the single high-level criterion used in evaluation. Both the ground-breaking nature/impact of the research and the PI’s ability to carry it out are assessed. Familiarize yourself with the sub-criteria for both dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility: Address important challenges; Ambitious objectives & beyond the state of the art; ambitious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state which important challenges will be tackled, what the ground‑breaking or novel aspects are, and why objectives are ambitious but feasible. Avoid portraying the project as merely incremental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — scientific approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific approach: Feasibility; Appropriateness of research methodology to achieve goals; Timescales, resources & PI time commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors judge whether the approach is feasible given the ambition, whether methods and working arrangements are appropriate, and whether timescales/resources/PI commitment are adequate and justified. Include clear methods, work plan, risk assessment and resource justification (based on the full proposal/Part II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to conduct ground-breaking research; Evidence of creative independent thinking; Scientific expertise & capacity to execute the project; (AdG) leadership in training and advancement of young scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate creative independent thinking and the scientific track record/skills needed to execute the project. For Advanced Grants include leadership and mentoring record. Use CV/track record section to provide concrete evidence (publications, leadership roles, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sub‑criterion: Intellectual capacity and creativity (explicit questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project? To what extent has the PI demonstrated sound leadership in the training and advancement of young scientists? (AdG)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer these specific questions in the proposal narrative and CV. Give evidence rather than generic claims (e.g., concrete examples of independent work, key publications, leadership roles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sub‑criterion: Ground‑breaking nature and potential impact (explicit questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the importance and novelty early and clearly—explain novelty relative to state‑of‑the‑art and interdisciplinary contributions where relevant. Describe potential impact on the research field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sub‑criterion: Scientific approach (explicit questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the proposed project (based on the Extended Synopsis)? To what extent are the proposed research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals (based on the full Scientific Proposal)? To what extent are the proposed timescales, resources and PI commitment adequate and properly justified (based on the full Scientific Proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish what is stated in Part I (Extended Synopsis) vs Part II (full implementation). Provide a clear work plan, milestones, risk management and justification of resources and time commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility assessment at Step 1 (procedural rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the new proposal structure Part I (5 pages) contains overall idea & objectives, current state of the art, research strategy and impact; feasibility is no longer assessed at Step 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Part I focuses on idea, novelty and impact. Detailed feasibility evidence will be evaluated in Step 2 with Part II, so do not overload Part I with feasibility detail that won’t be assessed in Step 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and clarity for non‑experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be understandable for non‑experts of your field; leave no question and no evaluation criterion unanswered. Use concise title, headings, sub‑headings, clear comprehensible language, and short sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for panel members who may not be specialists in your narrow subfield. Use paragraphs, bullet points, tables, graphics (time chart, roles of team members, etc.) to improve clarity and navigation. Avoid confusingly written prose — reviewers penalize lack of clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure, formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Stick to the structure of the proposal and consider the evaluation criteria. Respect formatting rules and page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed proposal template and strictly obey page limits (Part I: 5 pages; Part II: 7 pages for StG/CoG in WP2026 as per new structure). Non‑compliance can harm assessment or lead to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of required administrative and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Forms/Proposal Submission Forms (General Information, Participants & Contacts, Budget + Resources description, Ethics and security, other call specific questions); Part I (B1, 5 pages); CV + Track record (4 pages); Part II (B2, 7 pages) + Funding ID; Host Support Letter (Host Institution Binding Statement of Support); PhD certificate/ PhD defence (StG/CoG); Further documents (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and upload all required documents. Host institution support and proof of PhD (where required) are essential for eligibility. Ensure budget and ethics sections are complete and consistent with the proposal narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel selection and reviewer exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants choose a panel and indicate one or more keywords. Panels are organized in three scientific domains (PE, LS, SH). Up to three reviewers can be excluded in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the most appropriate panel and provide accurate keywords to help assignment. If there are potential conflicts or seriously unsuitable reviewers, use the reviewer exclusion option (max 3) with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process flow and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1 (remote) evaluation of Part I by panel members; 1st panel meeting; max. 44 proposals per panel pass to Step 2; individual assessment of full proposals by panel members & referees; 2nd panel meeting with INTERVIEWS of applicants; panel chairs’ meeting consolidation of domain rank lists; proposals selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that Step 1 uses the short Part I and is used to select proposals for in‑depth review; only a limited number (≈44) pass per panel. Prepare Part I to convince remote reviewers to invite you to Step 2, and be prepared for interviews in Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring categories and re‑application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1 scores: A = excellent quality; B = high quality but not sufficient; C = insufficient. Step 2 scores: A = recommended for funding; B = not funded. Consequences: A – invited: moves to Step 2; A – not invited: no restriction for resubmission; B: suspended for one call year; C: suspended for two call years. Unfunded A & B: no restrictions for a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of scoring implications for eligibility to resubmit and suspension periods. Aim for an A at Step 1 to be considered at Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected PI profile by grant type (Advanced Grant - AdG)
rubrics_metrics.description: AdG: 10 year track‑record of significant research achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For AdG applications emphasize a long record of high‑impact achievements and leadership; provide concrete evidence in CV and track record section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected PI profile by grant type (Consolidator Grant - CoG)
rubrics_metrics.description: CoG: Research independence & evidence of maturity; promising track record of early achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show clear signs of research independence, leadership potential, and a promising body of early achievements; include independent outputs and leadership roles where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected PI profile by grant type (Starting Grant - StG)
rubrics_metrics.description: StG: Potential for research independence & evidence of maturity; promising track record of early achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate clear potential for independence and early achievements (e.g., first‑author papers, distinct independent ideas). Provide a concise track record appropriate to career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected PI profile by grant type (Synergy Grant - SyG)
rubrics_metrics.description: SyG: Competitive track records as appropriate to the career stage; ability to successfully bring together elements necessary to address the scope and complexity of the proposed research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Synergy grants demonstrate complementary expertise across team members, track records appropriate to each PI’s career stage, and a convincing plan for integration and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical weaknesses to avoid (anti‑patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of common negative reviewer comments: 'neither the lead question nor the approaches are clearly defined'; 'rather incremental than groundbreaking'; 'serious doubts about the independence of the PI'; 'Feasibility is hard to judge based on the information provided'; 'Confusingly written proposal'; 'There is hardly any form of work plan'; 'The novelty of insights is not always clear'; 'the principal investigator does not seem to have the capacity and is not prepared to execute the outlined project'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these example criticisms as a checklist to fix your proposal: clarify lead questions and approaches, demonstrate novelty and independence, provide clear feasibility evidence and a detailed work plan, and improve writing clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reasons for rejection (common fail factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the research project: Too narrow or too broad; The project is incremental research; It is collaborative research of several researchers; Not enough information (hypothesis, objectives, work plan); Insufficient risk management strategy. Based on the research profile: Insufficient track record; Insufficient potential/proof for independence; Insufficient experience leading projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these failure points explicitly: define scope, emphasize novelty, justify single‑PI vs collaborative nature if applicable, include clear hypothesis/objectives/work plan, present risk management, and bolster evidence of independence and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and budgetary clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational aspects to provide and justify: Position/salary, Career prospects, Teaching, Overhead 25%, Team recruitment, Contract/salary, Premises, Depreciation, co‑financing, purchase, Equipment, After the project, Third Parties, Subcontracts, Associated Partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work closely with your host institution for realistic budget planning. Provide transparent justification for personnel, equipment, overheads and third‑party arrangements; ensure budget aligns with the described work plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI time commitment expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: PI time commitment to project (percentage/time) is assessed and must be adequate; different schemes have expected PI time commitments (table of percentages per grant type shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and justify the PI’s commitment, and, if required, the percentage devoted within EU/Associated Countries. Ensure host institution confirms allowable time commitment in the binding statement of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility rules and special provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility notes: victims of gender‑based (or any other kind of) violence may obtain an extension of their period following PhD for StG/CoG applicants; additional funding: researchers currently based outside Europe may request up to EUR 2 million (StG/CoG/AdG) which may be used for personnel costs; new 2027 eligibility rules (StG immediately after PhD within following 10 years; CoG between 5 and 15 years after PhD); researchers will be awarded no more than one Starting Grant and one Consolidator Grant during their career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check specific eligibility rules and special extensions early (work programme updates may appear). If eligible for extensions or additional funding, document and justify these in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal preparation: part‑specific focus (Part I vs Part II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I (Extended Synopsis/B1) — 5 pages: overall idea & objectives, current state of the art, research strategy and impact. Part II (former B2) — 7 pages: implementation (methods, work plan, risk assessment). CV + Track record (4 pages) separate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Part I to present the vision, novelty and impact concisely for Step 1 reviewers; use Part II to present detailed implementation, methods, timeline and risk mitigation for Step 2 evaluators. Keep each part within page limits and in the prescribed sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview and panel expectations in Step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2 includes interviews of applicants during the second panel meeting; reviewers expect clarity on ambition, feasibility, and PI suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for interviews by being able to succinctly explain novelty, feasibility, team roles and risk management. Practice answering weaknesses identified in the written proposal.
